quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge how far away vehicles are. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle in front of you. It may take longer to notice when the vehicle ahead stops, so you need extra time to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Meet U.S. DOT standards.
Fit snugly.
Have visible damage.
Have been worn during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn during a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly, and has no visible damage. If a helmet is worn during a crash, replace it immediately.

questions.question: When it is raining, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
Faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery, especially at the start of rain when oil from cars has not washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Go faster.
Follow closer behind other vehicles.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your distance from other vehicles at night. Use the headlights of the vehicle ahead to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors, why should you practice using them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
They make objects look closer than they actually are.
It is difficult to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to them.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same position in the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Change your lane position as conditions change on the road and in traffic.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals that there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn to make the bike lean the right way.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is used.
Remembers how hard the rider usually brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Read your owner's manual to understand how your motorcycle's braking system works.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Speed up while the brake is still engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks up, release the brake to regain control. However, if the rear wheel locks on a surface with good traction, you can keep the brake applied until you stop completely.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Dark or drab colors are harder to see.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At speeds greater than 55 mph.
After several hours of riding.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks on good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Normally, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes stopping especially hard for motorcycles.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When shifting into neutral.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly if a car is following too closely. The driver may not see hazards ahead that you are avoiding.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Do not use your headlight.
Switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag, over or in front of the rear axle. Placing the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. These are regulatory signs that you must follow.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.
Apply only the rear brake.
Apply only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten your motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly, reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far back on the motorcycle as possible.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on the motorcycle only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the operator's control. They should hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It uses less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to split up.
Riders in a close group reach their destination faster than riders in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders in a close group reach their destination faster than riders in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than riding spread out because the group uses less road space, is easier to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights and during passes. Riding close does not make you arrive faster.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly and gradually increase pressure on the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect blood alcohol content: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have an effect. How often someone drinks does not affect their BAC.

questions.question: As an operator, you should prepare a passenger to ride by instructing them to do each of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts. They should NOT maintain a large distance from you.
